title: Cite Or Lie
problem: Every AEO tool - including Mimos - has the same hidden bug: when an LLM cites a domain, it might be citing (a) a retrieval surfaced by the answer engine's grounding (Bing / Perplexity index), (b) a training set memorization, or (c) a generation hallucination with a plausible looking URL. For a regulated wealth management or telehealth firm, distinction (a) vs. (c) is the difference between "we're winning AI search" and "we have a compliance incident in the making.
direction: A grounded citation auditor for AI answer engines: every claimed citation in a Mimos report is verified against the answer engine's own retrieval trace (when available) and a deterministic re prompt protocol, returning a per citation (grounded | memorized | hallucinated) verdict with confidence - the compliance substrate AEO has been missing.
why: cite or lie won't. It positions Mimos's compliance moat as measurable. Until now the compliance pitch is qualitative. The grounded citation verdict turns it into a defensible number a GC can sign off on.
